title: Deadpan, pince-sans-rire, understatement, and litotes — lexical records (Wikipedia + Wiktionary)

verification.verification_notes: TIER 5 — audience/community-adjacent reference; NEVER sole support for any claim (layer0 tier rules). Accessed 2026-09-24. Contents: (a) Wikipedia 'Deadpan' wikitext — 1928 New York Times 'Slang of Film Men' item (Frank J. Wilstach) defining dead pan as 'playing a role with expressionless face, as, for instance, the work of Buster Keaton' [short PD fragment, quotable]; Bresnahan 1915 attestation of 'the dead pan'; etymology dead + pan (face); T.W. Barrett music-hall precedent relayed via Busby 1976. (b) Wiktionary 'deadpan', 'litotes', 'understatement', 'pince-sans-rire' — French equivalent confirmed: adjective 'dry, deadpan'; noun for a person with a deadpan sense of humour; literal gloss 'pinch without laughing'. (c) Wikipedia's note that 'A Modest Proposal' is conventionally an allusion to this style of deadpan satire, recorded under src-deadpan-modest-proposal-1729. Used only for recognition, vocabulary, and the cross-cultural lexical survey (§E); every claim it supports carries at least one tier 1–3 co-support.

limitations: French lexical items (pince-sans-rire) are recorded from English-language Wiktionary entries — gloss level only.
